description: Synthetic Fowler-pattern PRECISION fixture (clean baseline). A deliberately well-factored ~60-line notification module that contains structures which LOOK extractable but are NOT deepening opportunities: (1) two send_* functions sharing thin requests.post plumbing (the DRY-vs-deepening trap — extracting a shared _post wrapper is shallow, no depth gain), (2) config-at-edge env reads (the correct pattern), (3) a minimal passthrough getter. A faithful skill run must return ZERO Strong/Worth-exploring candidates. This is the n=2 independent precision test for the DRY-is-not-deepening guard (ADR-0003) — does it GENERALIZE beyond reader-mcp, not just memorize it?
_line_ranges_verified: 2026-05-21 against the bundled fixture (58 lines): config-at-edge env reads 13-16, send_slack/send_telegram thin-plumbing 21-54, get_last_status passthrough 56-58.
_design_note_no_expected: Clean baseline — empty by design. A Strong or Worth-exploring candidate is a precision failure (hard avoidance violation). Up to 1 honestly-hedged Speculative overlapping an avoidance region is tolerated (speculative_overflags_max). The whole point: re-test the DRY-is-not-deepening guard on a FRESH module the skill author did not tune against.

expected_avoidances.looks_like: Module-level env-var reads (SLACK_WEBHOOK, TELEGRAM_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT, TIMEOUT_S)
expected_avoidances.why_not_flagged: Configuration-at-edge is the recommended pattern — read env once at import so the rest of the module is config-free. Flagging this would be the bug, not the code.

expected_avoidances.looks_like: send_slack() and send_telegram() share near-identical requests.post plumbing (build payload → POST with headers+timeout → status check → _last.update → raise on failure) — looks like extractable duplication
expected_avoidances.why_not_flagged: DRY ≠ deepening. A shared `_post(url, payload)` helper would be a SHALLOW wrapper over requests.post (interface ≈ implementation; requests.post is already the deep module) — duplication removal with no depth gain, below the threshold to flag. The two named functions also read better at call sites (different config preconditions, different payload shapes). A Speculative hedge here is a tolerated soft overflag; a Strong/Worth-exploring flag is a hard precision miss.

expected_avoidances.looks_like: get_last_status() returns dict(_last) — a one-line passthrough
expected_avoidances.why_not_flagged: It IS the module's minimal read interface (a defensive copy of the last-send state). Inlining `_last` access into callers would scatter the internal state shape and lose the copy boundary. Not a shallow module to delete — the minimal interface is correct.

expected_outcome_summary.verdict_if_within_limits: pass — skill correctly treats a fresh well-factored module as a clean baseline; the DRY-is-not-deepening guard generalizes (does not over-flag the shared requests.post plumbing).
